function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since ancient times.  Early observations were made by Thales of Miletus (circa 600 BCE) who noted that rubbing amber produced static charge.  In the 16th–17th centuries, William Gilbert coined the term “electricus” and studied magnetism and static electricity.  The 18th‑century experiments of Benjamin Franklin (e.g., his kite experiment) and Alessandro Volta (inventing the voltaic pile) laid the groundwork for modern electrical science.  Subsequent work by scientists such as Michael Faraday, André-Marie Ampère, and James Clerk Maxwell turned these observations into the physics of electricity we use today.
